name: gifcap
desc: Capture video from an Android device and make a gif
why: Turning a phone's live video into a gif from the terminal is a neat transform, though the idea is fairly simple.

brief.what_it_is: gifcap is a shell script that records the screen of a plugged-in Android device and turns the recording into a GIF. You run it with an output filename, reproduce the behaviour on the phone, and press CTRL+C to stop. The output is a GIF meant to be pasted straight into Slack. The README says the script uses adb, ffmpeg, and ffprobe, and mentions Android's screenrecord, which suggests it wraps those tools, though the README does not spell out the pipeline.
brief.why_it_exists: The author says a video is worth far more than a picture when prototyping animations or recording visual glitches, and that the script exists to make it easy to capture and share subtle app behaviour with a single command.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not describe the internal mechanism in detail. It names adb, ffmpeg, and ffprobe as dependencies and mentions screenrecord, which is consistent with capturing the device screen over adb and converting the video to GIF with ffmpeg. The bash script itself is the whole program.

commands_seen.context: Usage: starts a recording to the named GIF file; press CTRL+C to stop recording.
macOS install variant that also has Homebrew set up the Android SDK, for users who don't already have one.

brief.install_notes: On macOS, brew install gifcap, and the README assumes adb is already on your PATH unless you use the --with-android-sdk flag. On other systems, make sure adb, ffmpeg, and ffprobe are on your $PATH, your console can run bash, and then copy the gifcap script somewhere on your $PATH. You need a real Android device plugged in because emulators generally don't have screenrecord built in.
brief.standout: It is a small bash script that turns a phone's live screen into a Slack-ready GIF with one command, aimed at sharing app glitches and animation behaviour rather than producing a polished media tool. The Homebrew flag that installs the Android SDK for you is a convenience touch.
brief.status: unknown. The fetched README shows no release dates, version numbers, or recent-commit information, so I could not judge whether the project is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: Requires a physical Android device; emulators are not supported for this. Needs adb, ffmpeg, and ffprobe installed by hand outside macOS. Needs bash. The README's copyright line names Microsoft Corporation, but the fetched page includes no license text, so licensing is unclear from what I read. The brew_caveats field was empty.
quotes: A picture is worth 1,000 words - and, when prototyping animations, recording visual glitches, etc, a video is worth far more.
This script makes it easy to capture and share subtle app behavior by producing ready-to-paste-in-Slack GIFs with a single command.
Note: you'll need an actual Android device plugged in - emulators don't generally have `screenrecord` built in.
